analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only, and no code, protocol schema, key handling or trust-boundary behavior is changed in what was supplied.

1. docs/reference/configuration.md line 329 adds a row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES. It is a default-on estimator correction (per-batch decode charging, anchored isolated-prefill rate, newest-observation freshness). Setting it off restores the previous estimators, and it is forwarded to the launchd provider job.
- It touches deadline admission on the provider, which is an availability and scheduling concern (TB-002, T-010). It does not touch confidentiality, attestation or authorization.
- The environment variable is a local operator control. The operator is the adversary in ADV-001, but the variable only changes the provider's own admission estimates and does not grant serving permission (T-052/T-053 are untouched).
- One residual question: an under-charged decode projection could admit work that misses its deadline. That is a performance matter, not a security regression. I did not see the implementing Swift code, so I cannot verify the claim.

2. docs/reference/prediction-decision-telemetry.md only adds a paragraph and updates the date. It states that wire fields are unchanged. The projected_decode_tokens semantics for MTP engines are described, and profile contents are not expanded. There is no new identity or prompt data, so there is no T-058 impact.

3. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md clarifies how sample_age_ms is computed (age since the newest observation) and how the Swift producer applies it per bucket. Wire fields are unchanged. Coordinator-side trust in provider-self-reported timing is a pre-existing contract.

I saw no changes to the prefix-cache threat T-041, to encryption, or to attestation. The implementing source files, such as AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, were not supplied, so the documented behavior is unverified against code. This is a coverage limit and not evidence of a flaw. No threat-model update appears necessary.
